question: Should durable publisher-feed state and scheduling become a core `src/plugins` control-plane responsibility before the RFC, producer, and prerequisite consumer stack are accepted?
rationale: The patch commits OpenClaw to a new shared persistent model and signed remote-feed trust boundary; code review cannot determine that permanent ownership and landing order without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the core stack after repair
options.body: Confirm core ownership, require monotonic transactional writes and upgrade/live proof, then review the prerequisite stack in landing order.

options.title: Keep transport outside core
options.body: Move publisher-specific persistence and scheduling to the owning plugin or ClawHub integration while retaining only a generic core seam if one is demonstrably missing.

options.title: Pause pending protocol adoption
options.body: Leave the draft stack paused until the RFC and producer contracts are accepted and stable enough to implement against.

recommendation.title: Approve the core stack after repair
recommendation.body: Confirm core ownership, require monotonic transactional writes and upgrade/live proof, then review the prerequisite stack in landing order.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans shared state, plugin control-plane ownership, and acceptance of a new remote trust surface.
